messages:
elaine_support: Customer (ACME Retail) opened a ticket: sudden spike in API 5xxs and 300-500ms extra latency. They say traffic originating from their on‑prem gateway is being routed to eu-central proxies instead of us-west.

sam_support: Copying logs they attached. quick summary: high p50/p95 for generation endpoint from last 30m, and many connections to eu hub IPs. No config changes on their side in the last 24h.

elaine_support: @raj_oncall can you pick this up? customer is high-priority and on Dedicated + Private.

raj_oncall: On it. Initial hypothesis: some healthcheck/failover flipped region affinity and sessions got sticky to eu. Asking for packet captures and egress NAT mapping from the customer.

sam_support: Asked customer to run these repro steps on their bastion and paste results: ```bash
curl -v -H 'Host: api.redwood' http://10.10.8.4:8080/health
sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 10.10.8.4 and port 8080 -c 200 -w /tmp/egress.pcap
``` They returned a short tcpdump and curl -v. Included snippet: "Connected to 10.10.8.4 (10.10.8.4) port 8080... > GET /health HTTP/1.1\n< HTTP/1.1 200 OK" but src IPs in tcpdump show SNAT to 34.72.11.9 (eu hub).

talia_net: Interesting — that SNAT IP is an eu-hub NAT egress. Two things jump out: 1) their TGW/VPC routing path includes a peered hub that does east-west fallback, 2) our probe/healthchecks on the us-west proxy were intermittently marking us-west unhealthy due to ICMP probes being dropped by a firewall between customer and us-west. When LB health is flaky the routing can prefer fallback path through peered hub (eu).

raj_oncall: Confirming from infra: between 17:40-17:52 we saw flaps on the us-west proxy cluster where the healthcheck failure rate spiked. The healthchecks we run are currently ICMP-only for the peering path -> if ICMP is filtered by an intermediate firewall, the cluster becomes marked unhealthy even if app traffic/tcp is fine. That triggered failover to alternate peering (eu) for that customer prefix.

elaine_support: That explains the wrong region routing and the increased latency/5xxs (timeouts from cross-region path). Customer says they didn't change firewall rules though — could be transient filtering or a partner transit change.

sam_support: Customer ran a tcpdump filtered on 34.72.11.9 and showed persistent SYNs/TCP to eu IP after the flap. They also reported a billing alert from their end due to cross-region egress spikes.

talia_net: Short term mitigation: set their egress policy to prefer sticky-region affinity and disable cross-region failover for the affected CIDR (we can apply per-tenant routing override). Also we should switch our peering healthchecks to TCP/HTTP for the control plane so ICMP drops don't mark us down.

raj_oncall: I can apply a temporary per-tenant override to force us-west prefer and preserve source port NAT on next config push. Will also open a ticket with infra team to change probe type and add a more conservative failure threshold.

elaine_support: Thanks. Patch plan?

raj_oncall: Plan: 1) Apply tenant routing override (no cross-region failover) — immediate (5m). 2) Enable NAT source-port preservation for that tenant's prefix to avoid session breakage (10m). 3) Change probe type from ICMP to TCP/HTTP for peering healthchecks (infra change, scheduled, ETA 6h). 4) Postmortem with customer and network partner (tomorrow).

sam_support: Ran the override, customer confirms requests are now hitting us-west IPs again. p50 back to normal, p95 dropping. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy-rollout: tenant-route-override applied by raj_oncall at 1789456398 — rollout 100% success.

elaine_support: Great. Follow-ups: (a) confirm infra probe change, (b) recommend customer whitelist ICMP between their edge and our us-west peering for redundancy (but not required), (c) update runbook to prefer TCP/HTTP probes for peering.

talia_net: I'll own the runbook edit and infra ticket. Will include commands and a sample tcpdump to look for: ```bash
sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 'dst 34.72.11.9 and tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn) != 0'
``` and NAT table check snippet: ```bash
sudo iptables -t nat -L -n | grep 34.72.11.9
```

raj_oncall: Noting for postmortem: root cause = ICMP-only peering healthcheck + intermediate firewall filtering -> false negative health -> cross-region failover + SNAT causing session mismatches and 5xxs.

elaine_support: Filing a high-level incident summary to customer and ops. Thanks team.

sam_support: Customer follow-up: they'd like a short note for billing team to explain cross-region egress spike due to failover. I'll draft and send after PM review.

ops-bot: incident-note: incident-1789456123 recorded by elaine_support at 1789456489

elaine_support: Closing thread once infra confirms probe change.
